claim_1.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of peripheral blood/PBMCs from 77 Zostavax-vaccinated adults collected at baseline (day 0) and days 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 showed weak CD8+ T cell responses but significant CD4+ T cell responses after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Since Zostavax® comprises a live-attenuated virus, we were surprised to observe a weak CD8+ T cell response in peripheral blood, as measured by the downregulation of the pro-survival molecule (Bcl2) and upregulation of Ki67 (expressed in proliferating cells, (Miller et al., 2008) (Figure 1B)
In contrast significant CD4+ T cell responses were detected in the majority of subjects (Figure 1B), consistent with a recent report (Qi et al., 2016).
The subjects’ blood samples were collected at baseline prior to vaccination and at days 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 90 and 180 post-vaccination (Figure 1A).

comparison.finding: after vaccination versus baseline (day 0), weak CD8+ T cell responses were observed, measured by Bcl2 downregulation and Ki67 upregulation, while significant CD4+ T cell responses were detected

claim_2.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of blood/PBMCs from young and elderly Zostavax-vaccinated adults showed an increase in CD4+CXCR5+CXCR3+ICOS+ T cells and significant increases in CD4+ T cells positive for IFN-γ, IL-4 and IL-21 after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0) in both age groups.

sources.quote: Figure 1C shows an increase in CD4+CXCR5+CXCR3+ICOS+ T cells after Zostavax® in both the young and elderly adults.
Significant increase in CD4+ T cells that are positive for IFN-γ, IL-4 and IL-21 were also detected, indicating a mixed Th1/Th2/Th21 profile (Figure 1C).

comparison.finding: both young and elderly Zostavax-vaccinated adults showed increases after vaccination versus baseline (day 0) in CD4+CXCR5+CXCR3+ICOS+ T cells and in CD4+ T cells positive for IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-21

claim_3.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from Zostavax-vaccinated adults showed that depletion of CD4+ T cells, but not CD8+ T cells, abolished IFN-γ production compared to undepleted cells.

sources.quote: Figure S1B shows that depletion of CD4+ T cells, but not of CD8+ T cells, abolished IFN-γ production in the ELISPOT assay.

claim_4.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from a subset of HLA-A2+ Zostavax-vaccinated individuals showed that CD8+ T cells did not respond to vaccine peptides except in two individuals compared to baseline responses.

sources.quote: Despite detectable VZV-specific CD8+ T cell responses at baseline, the CD8+ T cells did not respond to the vaccine peptides with the exception of two individuals (ZV113 and ZV118, Figure 1D).

claim_5.claim: Q-PCR analysis of whole blood from Zostavax-vaccinated adults collected through day 14 showed residual viral DNA in some subjects at day 1 (day 1), but only three subjects showed positive viral replication in blood, including both CD8+ responders.

sources.quote: when we examined VZV DNA in the blood, although residual amount of viral DNA was seen in some subjects at day 1 (Table S2), only three showed positive viral replication in the blood, including both the CD8+ responders (Figure 1D).

claim_6.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from Zostavax-vaccinated adults showed a transient peak of antigen-specific plasmablast cells 7 days after vaccination (day 7) compared to baseline (day 0), and this cellular response was higher in the younger group than in the elderly group.

sources.quote: We detected a transient peak of antigen-specific plasmablast cells 7 days after Zostavax® administration (Figure 1E), consistent with the plasmablast responses observed to other vaccines such as influenza (Wrammert et al., 2008).
The magnitude of this cellular response was higher in the younger group (Figure 1E), consistent with previous studies with influenza vaccine (Sasaki et al., 2011).

comparison.finding: baseline antigen-specific plasmablast cells measured at day 0 in younger and elderly groups
the magnitude of the antigen-specific plasmablast cellular response at day 7 was higher in the younger group than in the elderly group

claim_7.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from young and elderly Zostavax-vaccinated adults showed significant increases in VZV glycoprotein-specific IgG after vaccination in both groups compared to baseline (day 0), with IgG peaking between 2 and 4 weeks after vaccination (days 14–28) and dropping by day 180, and the younger group showing a greater increase than the elderly group.

sources.quote: The measurement of VZV glycoprotein-specific IgG over the course of the study showed significant increases induced by Zostavax® in both the young and elderly adults (Figure 1E).
The IgG antibody peaked between two and four weeks after vaccination, and dropped by 180 days after vaccination.
Direct comparison between the two groups indicates that the younger group had a greater increase of VZV-specific antibody after vaccination (Figure 1E).

comparison.finding: baseline comparison at day 0 between young and elderly Zostavax-vaccinated adults
younger group showed a greater increase in VZV glycoprotein-specific IgG than the elderly group at day 14 after vaccination
younger group showed a greater increase in VZV glycoprotein-specific IgG than the elderly group at day 28 after vaccination
VZV glycoprotein-specific IgG had dropped by day 180 after vaccination in both groups, with the younger group showing a greater increase than the elderly group overall

claim_8.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from young and elderly Zostavax-vaccinated adults showed VZV-specific IgA was significantly increased in both groups after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0), with no significant difference between young and elderly groups.

sources.quote: we measured plasma VZV-specific IgA, which was significantly increased in both groups. However, there was not a significant difference between the young and elderly groups (Figure S1E).

comparison.finding: no significant difference in VZV-specific IgA between young and elderly groups at baseline
no significant difference in VZV-specific IgA between young and elderly groups after vaccination

claim_9.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from Zostavax-vaccinated adults showed interferon-induced antiviral genes including MX1 and IFI44L and PSPH were highly upregulated at day 1 relative to baseline (day 0), while immunoglobulin genes, TNFRSF17 and MZB1 were highly upregulated at day 7 relative to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: We assessed the gene expression changes in PBMCsinduced by Zostavax® vaccination. Besides the interferon induced antiviral genes, such as MX1 and IFI44L, a phosphoserine phosphatase, PSPH, was highly upregulated at day 1/0 and day 3/0 (Figure S2A).

At day 7, immunoglobulin genes were highly upregulated, as well as TNFRSF17 and MZB1, two genes extensively reported for their roles in antibody production (Li et al., 2014; Nakaya et al., 2011; Querec et al., 2009) (Figure S2A).

comparison.finding: interferon-induced antiviral genes including MX1 and IFI44L and PSPH were highly upregulated at day 1 relative to baseline
immunoglobulin genes, TNFRSF17 and MZB1 were highly upregulated at day 7 relative to baseline

claim_10.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from Zostavax-vaccinated adults showed a strong plasmablast signature at day 7 relative to baseline (day 0), while several innate immunity modules related to antigen presentation, dendritic cells, cytosolic DNA sensing, RIG-I receptor signaling and type I IFN responses were weakly induced compared to YF-17D.

sources.quote: BTM analysis of the response to Zostavax® revealed signatures seen with several other vaccines, including the seasonal influenza vaccines and the meningococcal vaccine such as a strong plasmablast signature at day 7 (Figure S2B), consistent with the robust plasmablast response at this time point (Figure 1E).

Surprisingly however, several BTMs related to innate immunity including those relating to antigen presentation, dendritic cells, antiviral innate immune sensing including cytosolic DNA sensing, RIG-I receptor signaling and type I IFN responses were weakly induced by Zostavax® relative to YF-17D, which is another live viral vector (Figure S2B).

comparison.finding: strong plasmablast signature at day 7 relative to baseline (day 0)

claim_11.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of in vitro stimulated PBMCs from healthy donors showed Zostavax infected a substantial proportion of monocytes, myeloid DCs and plasmacytoid DCs but failed to activate these cells, as evidenced by failure to upregulate CD80 and failure to induce IFNα in pDCs or IL-6 in monocytes or mDCs compared to stimulated controls.

sources.quote: We could detect VZV glycoprotein in a substantial proportion of monocytes, myeloid DC (mDC) and plasmacytoid DC (pDC) by intracellular FACS staining, suggesting uptake of virus by these cells (Figure S3A).
However, there did not appear to be activation of these cell types in response to stimulation of PBMCs with Zostavax®, as evidenced by the failure to upregulate CD80 (Figure S3A)
Intracellular FACS staining of cytokines in these cultures revealed that Zostavax® failed to induce IFNα in pDCs (Figure S3C) or IL-6 in monocytes or mDCs (Figure S3D).

claim_12.claim: Cytokine Bead Array (CBA) analysis of cell-free culture supernatants from in vitro stimulated PBMCs showed Zostavax induced several chemokines, including CXCL8, CCL2, CXCL9 and CXCL10, compared to unstimulated cultures.

sources.quote: However, Zostavax® induced several chemokines, such as CXCL8, CCL2, CXCL9 and CXCL10 in PBMCs (Figure S3E).

comparison.finding: Zostavax induced several chemokines, including CXCL8, CCL2, CXCL9 and CXCL10, compared to unstimulated cultures

claim_13.claim: Plasma Metabolomics analysis of plasma from vaccinees showed the largest numbers of differential metabolites at day 1 relative to baseline (day 0) and at day 14 relative to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Compared to the baseline, both negative and positive ionization data indicated the largest numbers of differential metabolites at day 1 and day 14 (under negative ionization, 429 and 425 peaks at FDR < 0.1, respectively).

comparison.finding: the largest numbers of differential metabolites were observed at day 1 relative to baseline
the largest numbers of differential metabolites were observed at day 14 relative to baseline

claim_14.claim: Plasma Metabolomics analysis of plasma from Zostavax-vaccinated adults showed day 1 relative to baseline (day 0) significant metabolic pathways including TCA cycle and propanoate metabolism, and these pathways were also identified in day 3 PBMC transcriptional data.

sources.quote: We used the mummichog software, a pathway tool designed for untargeted metabolomics data (Li et al., 2013), to evaluate the day 1/0 significant metabolic pathways shown in Figure 2C. Strikingly, TCA cycle (and overlapping glycolysis and gluconeogenesis) and propanoate metabolism was also identified in the day 3/0 transcriptomics data (Table S3).

comparison.finding: day 1 relative to baseline showed significant metabolic pathways including TCA cycle and propanoate metabolism
TCA cycle and propanoate metabolism were also identified in day 3 PBMC transcriptional data

claim_15.claim: Luminex xMAP analysis of plasma from young and elderly Zostavax-vaccinated adults showed higher IL-7 levels in the elderly group than in the young group at day 3 relative to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Among the few different networks at day 3/0 is an IL-7 cytokine network (Figure 4D).
Luminex data supported the higher level of IL-7 in the elderly group (Figure 4F).

comparison.finding: IL-7 levels were higher in the elderly group than in the young group at day 3 relative to baseline (day 0)

claim_16.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of blood cell populations from young and elderly Zostavax-vaccinated adults showed NK cell differences, with NK cells higher in the elderly group than in the young group before vaccination (day 0).

sources.quote: The most significant gene network consisted of gene modules related to inflammation, cytosolic DNA sensing and NK cells, which were significantly higher in the elderly group (Figure 4B)

Furthermore, difference in NK cells measured by flow cytometry (Figure 4E) was consistent with the transcriptomics data, and Luminex data supported the higher level of IL-7 in the elderly group (Figure 4F).

comparison.finding: NK cells were higher in the elderly group than in the young group before vaccination at day 0

claim_17.claim: Q-PCR analysis of whole blood from vaccinees showed that, if day 1 viral DNA was considered carryover, eight individuals were PCR+ for clear viral replication, and comparison with 27 PCR− individuals revealed significant differences at all time points.

sources.quote: If day 1 viral DNA is deemed as carryover from vaccine injection, eight individuals showed clear viral replication (PCR+).
The comparison between these 8 PCR+ subjects and 27 PCR− individuals revealed significant differences at all time points (Figure S6E).

comparison.finding: PCR+ individuals with clear viral replication differed significantly from PCR− individuals at all time points

claim_18.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs showed that PCR+ vaccinees had higher baseline plasma cell signature genes and BCR signaling, higher heme biosynthesis and inositol phosphate metabolism, and by day 7 relative to baseline (day 0) had higher cytoskeleton remodeling, cell adhesion, platelet activation and G protein mediated calcium signaling but lower plasma cell signature genes compared to PCR− vaccinees.

sources.quote: The PCR+ group had higher baseline levels of plasma cells signature genes and BCR signaling, although these signatures were unlikely to have derived from VZV specific plasmablasts; they also had higher gene expression for heme biosynthesis and inositol phosphate metabolism (Figure S6E).

By day 7/0, the PCR+ group had higher activity in cytoskeleton remodeling (enriched for SRF targets), cell adhesion, platelet activation and G protein mediated calcium signaling (Figure S6E), possibly indicative of a response to viral replication.
The PCR+ group also had lower activity in plasma cells signature genes at day 7/0 (Figure S6F), indicating a compromised antibody response.

comparison.finding: At baseline (day 0), PCR+ vaccinees had higher plasma cell signature genes, BCR signaling, heme biosynthesis, and inositol phosphate metabolism than PCR− vaccinees.
At day 7 relative to baseline, PCR+ vaccinees had higher cytoskeleton remodeling, cell adhesion, platelet activation, and G protein mediated calcium signaling than PCR− vaccinees.
At day 7 relative to baseline, PCR+ vaccinees had lower plasma cell signature genes than PCR− vaccinees.

claim_19.claim: Luminex xMAP analysis of plasma showed day 7 relative to baseline (day 0) RANTES was significantly higher in PCR− vaccinees than in PCR+ vaccinees.

sources.quote: Interestingly, the day 7/0 cytokine RANTES is significantly higher in the PCR− group (Figure S6F).

comparison.finding: RANTES was significantly higher in PCR− vaccinees than in PCR+ vaccinees at day 7 relative to baseline

claim_20.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of blood cell populations showed that day 7 relative to baseline (day 0) IFN-γ+ T cells were the most significant predictors of day 28 relative to baseline (day 0) IgG response.

sources.quote: Among the cell populations, day 7 IFN-γ+ T cells are the most significant predictor of IgG response (Figure S7B).

comparison.finding: day 7 relative to baseline IFN-γ+ T cells were the most significant predictors of day 28 relative to baseline IgG response
day 28 IgG response was evaluated relative to baseline

claim_21.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs showed that day 3 relative to baseline (day 0) SREBF1 target genes predicted Tfh response, while day 7 relative to baseline (day 0) SREBF1 target genes predicted antibody response.

sources.quote: In this study, we found that day 3/0 SREBF1 targets was predictive of Tfh response (Figure 6A), and day 7/0 SREBF1 targets was predictive of antibody response (Figure 6B).

comparison.finding: day 3 relative to baseline SREBF1 target genes predicted Tfh response
day 7 relative to baseline SREBF1 target genes predicted antibody response

claim_22.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs showed that a gene module of inositol phosphate metabolism at day 1 relative to baseline (day 0) was a significant predictor of T cell response.

sources.quote: A gene module of inositol phosphate metabolism (M129, day 1/0) is a significant predictor of T cell response (Table S5).

comparison.finding: The inositol phosphate metabolism gene module (M129) at day 1 relative to day 0 was a significant predictor of T cell response.

claim_23.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs identified subject groups with low or high inositol phosphate metabolism across time points, and the high inositol phosphate metabolism group showed high expression of immunoglobulins at day 1 relative to baseline (day 0) but low expression at day 7 relative to baseline (day 0), with significantly lower numbers of activated CD4+ T cells than the low inositol phosphate metabolism group.

sources.quote: Combining data from all time points, groups of subjects of low or high IP metabolism emerged from unsupervised clustering (Figure 7D).
the group of high IP metabolism showed high expression of immunoglobulins at day 1/0, but low expression at day 7/0 (Figure 7D–E).
Similarly, the group of high IP metabolism had significantly lower number of activated CD4+ T cells (Figure 7F).

comparison.finding: the high inositol phosphate metabolism group had significantly lower numbers of activated CD4+ T cells than the low inositol phosphate metabolism group

claim_24.claim: Plasma Metabolomics analysis of plasma showed that the high inositol phosphate metabolism group had lower levels of plasma metabolite cluster Neg257, tentatively matched to glycerophospholipids, compared to the low inositol phosphate metabolism group.

sources.quote: Lower level of plasma metabolite cluster Neg257, which is tentatively matched to glycerophospholipids, was also seen in this group, together with differences in neutrophils and cytokines (Figure 7F).

comparison.finding: the high inositol phosphate metabolism group had lower levels of plasma metabolite cluster Neg257, tentatively matched to glycerophospholipids, than the low inositol phosphate metabolism group
